claim.quote: measure the τ mass to be 1777.09 ± 0.08 ± 0.11 MeV/c2 , where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. This result is the most precise to date.

date.note: arXiv submission date (30 May 2023). The arXiv abstract page carried no journal reference when read, so the record is a preprint.

name: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass
notes: Journal publication was not confirmed on a source fetched in this session.

significance.note: Not applicable: a precision measurement, not a discovery claim; no significance is quoted.

summary.plain: Belle II measured the mass of the tau lepton, one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model, and states in its abstract that the result is the most precise to date.
summary.technical: Pseudomass-endpoint measurement in τ⁻ → π⁻π⁺π⁻ ν_τ using ~175 million e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ events in 190 fb⁻¹ at √s = 10.579 GeV, giving m_τ = 1777.09 ± 0.08(stat) ± 0.11(syst) MeV/c².

title: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass with the Belle II experiment
why_it_matters: The paper says the tau mass is one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model, that a precise value matters for tests of lepton-flavour universality between the tau and lighter leptons (the tau mass enters to the fifth power), for predictions of the tau's branching fractions, and for determining the strong-interaction coupling at the tau-mass scale.
